review_notes: Read all 362 lines of the target, plus the neighbouring API in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Fold.lean (foldr/foldr' simp lemmas) and the only external consumer of the target declarations, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Inversion.lean (line 64). Grepped Mathlib for uses of contractLeft/contractRight/equivExterior (only Inversion.lean and this file) and for changeFormEquiv_apply/equivExterior_apply (no hits, i.e. there is no application lemma for equivExterior anywhere). The main finding is the simp attribute on the def equivExterior together with the silenced simpNF failure; the second is the missing simp rules for the nilpotency composites of the two contractions. I could not execute Lean, so I do not claim to have observed a simpNF failure, a loop, or that the proposed `@[simps! apply]`/`[simp]` attributes compile; the benefit of adding `[simp]` to contractLeft_contractLeft/contractRight_contractRight is based on the orientation (LHS strictly larger, RHS a literal 0) and on the absence of any competing simp rule (contractLeft_comm/contractRight_comm are not simp), not on a test. The direction of the remaining changeForm lemmas (changeForm_ι_mul, changeForm_contractLeft, changeForm_changeForm) was considered and judged reasonably left non-simp because they expand the term.

findings.problem: The `@[simp]` attribute is placed on the definition, so the rule that enters the global simp set is the definition-unfolding equation `equivExterior.eq_1` (exactly the name used by the `nolint` on line 356), whose left-hand side is the bare constant `equivExterior`. Such a rule rewrites `equivExterior Q` to `changeFormEquiv changeForm.associated_neg_proof` in every context, e.g. inside `(equivExterior Q).toLinearMap` (Inversion.lean:64) and `(equivExterior Q).symm` (line 360), instead of performing the intended single step on an application; the normal form is only reached after a further rewrite by `changeFormEquiv_apply`, which `@[simps apply]` on `changeFormEquiv` (line 327) already provides. There is no application lemma `equivExterior_apply`/`equivExterior_symm_apply`, and the file acknowledges the interface is unverified (`#adaptation_note` plus `attribute [nolint simpNF] equivExterior.eq_1`), i.e. a linter failure is suppressed rather than fixed.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from the def and delete the `#adaptation_note` and `attribute [nolint simpNF] equivExterior.eq_1`; instead annotate the def so that a specific application rewrite is generated, e.g. `@[simps! apply] def equivExterior ...`, or add explicit lemmas (suggested statements, untested) `@[simp] theorem equivExterior_apply (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) : equivExterior Q x = changeForm changeForm.associated_neg_proof x` and the analogous symm lemma, and check that any downstream `by simp` (Inversion.lean:64) still closes through them.
findings.benefit: The simp set then contains a canonical, checkable rewrite with an application-shaped left-hand side instead of a wholesale definition unfolding; the simpNF suppression and its adaptation note disappear, and users get an `equivExterior_apply` lemma to compute the isomorphism on elements rather than having to unfold the whole `LinearEquiv`.

findings.problem: The simp interface of the contraction API covers the base cases (`contractLeft_ι`, `contractLeft_algebraMap`, `contractLeft_one`, and the `contractRight` analogues, lines 153-181) but not the nilpotency composites, so for an abstract multivector `x` an expression such as `d⌋(d⌋x)` or `x⌊d⌊d` does not reduce under `simp`, although `0` is the obvious normal form. The file itself has to fall back on `rw` for this: `changeFormAux_changeFormAux` needs `contractLeft_contractLeft` explicitly (line 230). Both statements are genuine reductions (the left-hand side is strictly larger than the right-hand side `0`), and there is no competing rule: `contractLeft_comm`/`contractRight_comm` (lines 198, 207) are not simp lemmas, so adding these rules cannot create a cycle.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `contractLeft_contractLeft` (line 186) and to `contractRight_contractRight` (line 194), leaving the statements unchanged. The rest of the file uses `simp only`/`simp_rw` with explicit lemma lists (lines 188, 200, 203, 291, 294) or `simpa only` (line 177), so its proofs are not exposed to the new rules; the single unrestricted `simp` (line 264) is about `QuadraticMap.toQuadraticMap_associated` and does not mention contractions.
findings.benefit: Goals of the form `d⌋(d⌋x) = 0` and `x⌊d⌊d = 0` for abstract multivectors, which are exactly the computations one performs with the contraction operators (and which the file currently closes by explicit `rw`), become closable by `simp`, completing the existing generator/scalar/`1` simp lemmas with the matching nilpotency step.
